title: Scheduling and Revaluing Items on the Larkspur Valuables Floater
content:
Larkspur Valuables Floater underwriting desk guidance: scheduling an item and raising its value.

## The scheduling rule

1. **Class and limits.** An item is scheduled only in a class the floater's tier schedules, for no more than the tier's largest scheduled value for one item, and only while the schedule total stays within the tier's largest total scheduled value.
2. **Scheduled value.** The scheduled value is the appraised or purchase value rounded to the tier's rounding unit for scheduled values. The item's description is recorded exactly as it appears on the appraisal or bill of sale.
3. **Floater status.** Items are scheduled only while the floater is bound or in force. This is read from the floater's record: a floater whose status is cancelled or expired schedules nothing, and neither is a revaluation recorded on it.
4. **Appraisal documents.** An item valued above the tier's written-appraisal threshold is scheduled only on a written appraisal or bill of sale dated no earlier than the appraisal age limit that ends on the scheduling date. The appraisal age limit is counted in whole calendar years back from the scheduling date, and an appraisal dated exactly the tier's number of years earlier is still accepted. The appraisal date and the item description are those the named insured gives from the appraisal or bill of sale for that item.
5. **One entry per item; revaluation.** The same item is never scheduled twice; a higher value is recorded by revaluation on a new appraisal, and a revaluation never lowers a value (a lower value is a removal and a new scheduling). A revaluation records the increase in value, with the date of the new appraisal.

## Eligibility checklist for a new item

| Point | Satisfied when |
|---|---|
| Floater status | bound or in force |
| Class | listed among the classes the tier schedules |
| Single-item value | not more than the tier's single-item limit |
| Schedule total after adding the item | within the tier's schedule limit |
| Appraisal document (only above the threshold) | dated no earlier than the age limit ending on the scheduling date |
| Same item already on the schedule | no (a higher value goes by revaluation) |

## Boundary cases on the appraisal age (hypothetical dates)

A hypothetical Valuables Floater Preferred item valued above the Preferred threshold, scheduled on 12 May of a given year, where the Preferred age limit is 5 years:

- Appraisal dated 12 May five years earlier: exactly five calendar years back, accepted.
- Appraisal dated 11 May five years earlier: earlier than the limit, not accepted.

The same item scheduled on a Valuables Floater Select, whose age limit is 3 years, needs an appraisal dated no earlier than 12 May three years earlier.

## Value changes (hypothetical)

- A necklace scheduled at 6000 USD is re-appraised at 7500 USD: a revaluation records the 1500 USD increase.
- The same necklace re-appraised at 5200 USD: the value is not lowered by revaluation; the 6000 USD entry is removed and the necklace is scheduled again at 5200 USD.
